citations.M1: Add/migrate/drop are all scheduled in the same Thursday window with no soak time between migrate and contract; fix: split 0143 into its own deploy at least a day after the backfill is confirmed reconciled.
citations.M2: `service.py`'s INSERT no longer sets `status`, so every order created by new-code pods gets `status = NULL` and silently drops out of the finance export's `status IN ('paid','shipped')` filter from the moment the rolling deploy starts; fix: keep writing both columns during the expand phase
citations.M4: `MAPPING` has no branch for `PAID`, `canceled` (one L), `complete`, or NULL status — 7,764 prod rows — so those rows stay `state IS NULL` forever
citations.M5: Backfill uses `OFFSET` against a `WHERE state IS NULL` filter that shrinks as rows get updated mid-run, so later batches skip unprocessed rows ... fix: paginate by keyset
citations.M6: The whole batch loop runs inside one outer `conn.transaction()`, so nothing is durably committed until the entire run finishes and a killed/timed-out job on 61M rows rolls back all progress ... fix: commit per batch.
citations.M7: `jobs/nightly_finance_export.py` reads `orders.status` directly and was missed because the grep was scoped to `app/`
citations.M8: Required gate between rollout steps 3 and 4: `SELECT count(*) FROM orders WHERE state IS NULL` must be 0 (or every remaining row explicitly triaged) before running 0143.
citations.M9: confirmed by the PR's own staging output (2,104,377 to backfill, only 1,055,000 updated)
citations.M10: 0143's `downgrade()` recreates `status` as an empty nullable Text column with no data mapped back from `state`; fix: map `state` back to the string by name in `downgrade`.
citations.M11: staging processed 2.1M rows (only half of those, per #1) in 11 min; prod is 61.4M rows, ~29x; fix: retime the corrected script against a prod-sized copy before trusting the window.
